_meta.purpose: FIRST EXECUTION of the eight-tier derivation (FOUNDATION §6). Not a calibration case — a live test of the procedure itself, run on a category where I have NOT read a delivered analysis.
_meta.why_this_category: CaiCa has a delivered analysis, so Sean can check this derivation against a finished expert product. But I derived it from the live web, not from the analysis — so the comparison is a genuine test rather than a replay.
_meta.method: Derived from the six form inputs using the six web-search results captured 2026-09-23. Not from the CaiCa analysis.
_meta.contains: derived tier set + which tiers the evidence supports vs which are inferred

form_inputs.what_you_sell: Bubble tea — hand-shaken milk tea and fruit tea drinks. 3 outlets, heartland and mall locations. Soy-milk-based line as a health positioning.
form_inputs.customer_job_best_endeavour: A treat drink — something cold, sweet and indulgent to pick up on the way somewhere or as a small daily reward. The healthy variant is 'a treat I don't feel guilty about'.
form_inputs.customer_and_trigger: Students, office workers and families passing a mall or MRT station. Trigger is proximity and impulse — walking past, or ordering on delivery for home.
form_inputs.claim: Singapore's first chain brewing tea with soy bean milk — a local, healthier bubble tea. Nutri-Grade B/C drinks.

derived_set.name: The Default
members: coffee or kopi at a hawker centre (~S$1.20-2.00)
canned or bottled drinks from a convenience store (~S$1.50-2.50)
derived_set.reason_to_purchase: Cheaper and requires no detour. The overwhelming majority of drink occasions resolve here — bubble tea is a treat, not a daily habit for most Singaporeans.
derived_set.evidence: inferred from the category's own structure: bubble tea is an indulgence purchase, and a treat category's default is always 'no treat'
derived_set.confidence: moderate — this is reasoning, not a fetched source

derived_set.name: The Cheap Substitute
members: R&B Tea (Large Fresh Milk from S$4.90)
derived_set.reason_to_purchase: Cheapest cup on the island. Mixue's standing prices need no app or membership — it is the answer to 'cheapest bubble tea in Singapore'. Its 30+ outlets sit in heartland malls, MRT stations and next to schools, exactly where a student or family would pass.
derived_set.price_floor: S$1.50 (Mixue King Cone), most drinks under S$3.50
derived_set.evidence: FETCHED — misslobang.com 2026 deals guide, price table
derived_set.note: This tier sets the floor that every other tier prices against. Note it sits BELOW the 'mid-tier' band the owner claims.

derived_set.name: The Direct Set
derived_set.reason_to_purchase: Same product, same occasion, already nearby. KOI is the widest network at 90 outlets (62 cafés + 26 Express counters inside MRT stations and hospitals) — reach, not novelty, is its advantage. CHAGEE is the fastest riser at 44, scaling from 36 in months. Chicha San Chen brews to order from its own Taiwan tea farms.
derived_set.evidence: FETCHED — outlet counts recounted from each brand's own store finder, 13 Sep 2026
derived_set.confidence: high for outlet counts (primary source: each brand's own site)
derived_set.note: 62+ bubble tea brands operate in Singapore. 953 bubble tea businesses islandwide (poidata, May 2026). This is a heavily fragmented tier — no single dominant player.

derived_set.name: The Category Incumbent — THE BLINDSPOT TIER
derived_set.reason_to_purchase: The owner frames this as a bubble tea category with a health angle. **The buyer is not shopping for 'bubble tea' — they are shopping for a treat drink, and the brand at the top of their mental list wins.** KOI is 'Singaporeans' favourite by polling' and the brand credited with starting the modern wave. CHAGEE reframed itself out of the category entirely: 'not a bubble tea brand, a tea expert' — original leaf tea, no powder, no creamer.
derived_set.evidence: FETCHED — misslobang polling/positioning claims; the CaiCa analysis independently found the same CHAGEE reframe
derived_set.confidence: moderate for the mental-ladder claim (no unaided-recall survey); high for the CHAGEE reframe (their own marketing)
derived_set.diagnostic_note: **The owner named no Tier 3 member.** Their claim is 'local + healthier'. Tier 3 shows the brands actually owning the treat-drink mind are imported (Taiwanese and Chinese), and the one that grew fastest did it by REJECTING the bubble tea label the owner is embracing. That is the blindspot.

derived_set.name: The Adjacent Crossover
members: convenience-store RTD tea (FairPrice now stocks CHAGEE teabags at S$12/8 = ~S$1.90 a home cup)
derived_set.reason_to_purchase: Takes the same treat-drink occasion with a different product. A S$6.50 coffee and a S$6.50 milk tea are the same purchase decision to a buyer who wants 'a nice cold drink'.
derived_set.evidence: FETCHED — the CHAGEE teabag shelf listing is a concrete crossover signal into retail
derived_set.note: This tier was NOT in the owner's frame, and it is where the wallet's real competition sits for the 'treat' job.

derived_set.name: The Professional Route
derived_set.evidence: no professional or institutional path exists for a beverage category
derived_set.note: Legitimately absent. The taxonomy predicts this — tier 5 only exists in regulated/high-trust categories.

derived_set.name: The Indirect
members: HPB Nutri-Grade regulation (a policy force, not a competitor — it constrains what can be claimed)
derived_set.reason_to_purchase: Not a purchase rival — a budget and behaviour dilutor. Health messaging reduces the number of treat occasions.
derived_set.note: Weakest tier in this derivation. Should be validated or dropped.

derived_set.name: The Emerging — WITHHELD (paid tier)
members: Molly Tea (茉莉奶白) — Shenzhen, flagship Orchard Central 6 Mar 2026, 18,000 cups in first 3 days, second CBD store 11 May 2026
Black Tree (上海泰茶) — 313@somerset, first outlet outside China
Tealive — Malaysian chain, single Changi T3 outlet since Jun 2025
Mr. Sun Tea — Taiwanese, at *SCAPE, trading since 1999
Gong Cha 2.0 — announced 2026 relaunch, global brand, not yet trading as at Sep 2026 (95% probability, per an independent case study)
Yi Fang Taiwan Fruit Tea — Punggol Coast Mall
derived_set.reason_to_purchase: New entrants arriving fast and at scale. Molly Tea sold 18,000 cups in three days and immediately opened a second, larger CBD store — it is the largest SE Asia store and the brand's largest CBD outlet worldwide.
derived_set.evidence: FETCHED — honeycombers review + misslobang arrival roundup
derived_set.confidence: high for the arrivals themselves (dates, addresses verified)
derived_set.note: WITHHELD from the free report per Sean's decision. Also NOTE: this was found by WEB SEARCH, not by the ACRA derivation — the ACRA path would be the systematic version and would catch entrants no roundup covers.

what_the_tiers_revealed_that_the_owner_d: The price floor is S$1.50, not the S$5.50 mid-tier the owner prices at — a 3.7x gap the owner did not acknowledge
The category is fragmented (62+ brands, 953 businesses) with NO dominant player — so 'competitive pressure' is not concentration, it is noise
Tier 3 is owned by imported brands (KOI/Taiwan, CHAGEE/China) while the owner's claim is 'local' — the localness claim is being made against a market that does not reward it
CHAGEE grew fastest by rejecting the bubble tea label; the owner is doubling down on it
Tier 4 (treat-drink crossover) was entirely absent from the owner's frame and is where the wallet competition actually sits
Tier 7 shows five+ arrivals in 12 months, including a Shenzhen chain that sold 18,000 cups in 3 days — the market is being invaded, not just competed in

checks_against_FOUNDATION_R.R3_tier3_from_buyers_category_word: PASS — derived from 'treat drink', not the seller's 'bubble tea'
checks_against_FOUNDATION_R.R5_owner_names_appear_in_result: PASS — the owner did not name competitors explicitly in the inputs, so this check could not run as designed. WEAKNESS.

honest_limits: Tier 0 rests on reasoning, not a fetched source
Tier 3's mental-ladder claim has no unaided-recall survey behind it — it is inferred from polling commentary
Tier 6 is weak and may not belong
Tier 7 here came from web search, not the ACRA derivation — so it is the less systematic version of the tier
No price was fetched for most Tier 2 members individually — only the Tier 1 floor and the owner's own price band are sourced
R5 could not run because the form inputs did not include the owner's named competitor list
_derivation_notes.unexpected_finding: The derivation produced a conclusion the inputs never hinted at: that the owner is competing on a claim ('local, healthier') that the market's own structure does not reward, while the fastest-growing player won by abandoning the category label entirely. That is the same shape of finding the CaiCa analysis reached — reached here from public data in six searches.
